subject: english
question: Select the sentence with no spelling errors.

options.text: Just who is crazy enough to go swimming when the pond across the street has a layer of ice across the top?
Just who is crezy enough to go swimming when the pond across the street has a layer of ice across the top?
Just who is crazy enough to go swiming when the pond across the street has a layer of ice across the top?
Just who is crazy enough to go swimming when the pond across the streat has a layer of ice across the top?

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"crazy"** means someone who is mentally deranged, especially as manifested in a wild or aggressive way. (पागल)

 
 
• **Example:** The idea of going bungee jumping without any safety gear is simply** crazy.**
 
 
 
• The word **"swimming"** refers to the sport or activity of moving through water by using the arms, legs, and body in motions called strokes. (तैराकी)
 
 
• **Example:** She enjoys **swimming** in the pool every morning as part of her exercise routine.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2** (crezy): This is a misspelling of "crazy".

 
 
• **Example:** The spelling "crezy" is incorrect; the correct spelling is "crazy".
 
 
 
• **Option 3** (swiming): This is a misspelling of "swimming".
 
 
• **Example:** The spelling "swiming" is incorrect; the correct spelling is "swimming".
 
 
 
• **Option 4** (streat): This is a misspelling of "street".
 
 
• **Example:** The spelling "streat" is incorrect; the correct spelling is "street".
